name: Project and Workspace Navigation
description: Presents the expandable, reorderable Project and Workspace hierarchy with consistent row, menu, selection, optional Environment connection status, and live Workspace Agent summaries.

states: Inspect expanded and collapsed Projects, active and default Workspace rows, and the nested hierarchy guide line.

Tab forward and backward through the Project create control and row options: each focused control appears immediately even when hidden at rest; inspect pointer hover and open-menu disclosure at wide and compact sizes.
Hover Project and Workspace rows, open their menus, right-click them, and inspect retained owner-row interaction states.
Open New Workspace and inspect existing Worktrees grouped under each represented Project repository before selecting one for direct Workspace creation.
Drag a Project between siblings and verify the pointer-following row, midpoint-driven sibling squeeze motion, edge scrolling, temporary collapse, and restoration after the drop.

Drag a Workspace between siblings inside one expanded Project and verify the same pointer-following, midpoint squeeze, release settlement, and cancellation behavior without changing Workspace activation or Project disclosure.
Inspect the Chinese Workspace menu opened by Shift+F10 without changing the active Workspace or Project disclosure.
Escape returns to that row's visible options trigger; repeat with the ContextMenu key and right-click, and verify that only one menu opens.
Use a real ContextMenu key down and up on a Project or Workspace: the browser's synthesized contextmenu event must not open a second surface, and one Escape dismisses the menu.
Open a management dialog or move focus outside the menu and verify that dismissal does not steal the new focus.
From the active terminal, press Ctrl+Shift+F6 to focus and reveal its offscreen current Workspace inside the Project scroll region without changing active location or Project disclosure.
At wide and compact sizes, verify that only the Project scroll region moves and outer Workbench and document scrolling remain unchanged; focusing an already visible row leaves scrollTop unchanged.
Scroll the focused row out of view, then make a new sidebar focus request and verify it is revealed again; focusing the standalone Terminal does not move the Project region.
From the active terminal, press Ctrl+Shift+F6 to focus and reveal the last Project representing its hidden active Workspace, preserving the collapsed state and active terminal.
Inspect Chinese focus and menu affordances at wide and compact sizes; the visible active Project takes precedence over the standalone Terminal fallback.
Compare a single provider summary, a two-provider overlapped summary, a three-provider generic Agent summary, and a Workspace with the default layout icon because it has no live Agent.
Inspect exact live Session counts independently from the number of distinct provider marks and verify attention, failure, working, success, and idle states use both a glyph and semantic color.
Inspect the expanded two-provider Workspace as a flat Agent-only list with provider and localized status on the first line and Tab, Panel, and primary or child terminal location on the second line.
Activate an enabled Agent row and verify exact Workspace, Tab, Panel, and terminal navigation; disabled rows remain perceivable but do not navigate.
Inspect a remote Project connection indicator and accessible status, then open Project options to inspect the explicit Connect action.
Change the deterministic capability state when exercising the component test to inspect pending, connected, retry, and disconnect projections.

useWhen: Workbench needs to show Project ownership, nested Workspace destinations, semantic menus, and Project ordering together.
A host needs the reviewed sidebar projection of Workbench Project and Workspace runtime state.
A person needs to notice live Agents in inactive Workspaces and navigate to an exact attached terminal without duplicating the Tab Strip.
A host supplies process-local Environment connection observations and explicit connect or disconnect commands for remote Projects.
avoidWhen: The hierarchy represents unrelated navigation entities that do not follow the Project and Workspace model.
The caller only needs a generic tree primitive or a flat destination list without Workbench actions.
invariants: Row options and Project creation remain reachable in both Tab directions, with immediate focus-within disclosure and no pointer hit target while hidden.

Exact row-local Shift+F10 and unmodified ContextMenu open the existing options dropdown for that row; composing, repeated, extra-modifier, and portaled-menu input never opens another menu or reaches a different object's actions.
Context-menu dismissal returns to the row's valid explicit options trigger through the shared primitive, while outside interaction, dialog handoff, and row removal cannot cause late focus theft.

A native keyboard contextmenu event from a row or the open dropdown identified by that row's exact trigger aria-controls cannot open a second menu; pointer context gestures and unrelated portal targets retain their existing behavior.

A new sidebar focus request resolves the current visible location, then the visible active Project representing a collapsed Workspace, then Terminal, without activating a location or expanding a Project.

Sidebar focus uses preventScroll and adjusts only the contained Project scroll owner's scrollTop to the nearer edge of its client viewport, clamped to the owner's scroll range; fully visible rows, oversized rows spanning the viewport, zero-height geometry, and Terminal cause no scroll.
Repeated sidebar request tokens and data changes alone do not move focus or scroll; a new request reveals its target even when it already has focus.
Selecting a Workspace changes the active terminal context while Project disclosure alone never changes it.
Pointer-clicking a Workspace row transfers focus to the exact destination terminal after activation and projection are ready, while keyboard and programmatic activation remain focus-neutral.
Active and hovered rows share the strong foreground role while default rows use the quieter foreground role.
An open row menu keeps the entire owner row highlighted without introducing a second trigger background.
Existing Worktree choices remain grouped by their represented repository, and selecting one creates no Workspace until host revalidation and canonical commit succeed.

Project and Workspace drag order is persisted only on release; the source row follows the pointer while crossed siblings squeeze into its vacated slot, and completion does not replay the previous displacement.
Workspace reordering remains inside the source Project and preserves active location, terminal ownership, Workspace identity, and Project disclosure.
A Workspace with no live Agent keeps the default layout icon and no Agent disclosure; retained ended Sessions never leave an Agent icon, count, status, or detail row.

A Workspace Agent summary counts deduplicated live Sessions, composes one or two curated provider identities, uses the generic Agent identity for three or more providers, and exposes its resolved status through text or an accessible label as well as color.

At most one Workspace Agent list is expanded across the sidebar; it is process-local, closes when its Project collapses or its final Agent ends, stays closed on activation and arrival, and is hidden during Workspace reorder.
Expanded Agent detail is a flat list only: it never repeats Tabs, terminal-only rows, panel thumbnails, prompts, commands, provider errors, or internal identifiers.

Agent-row navigation revalidates the latest live Session and focuses only the exact ready terminal projection; replacement, disappearance, rejection, or unrelated navigation cannot produce a late fallback focus.
Environment connection state is a host observation only; Workbench renders status and invokes explicit commands without owning SSH configuration, prompts, credentials, or runtime lifecycle.
